Output written to `/home/mara/cwe-bench/pipelines/stacking/out/screener-ds-rescreen/1961.json`.
Trust decision: OpenSSL decides the peer-certificate host identity inside `ssl.SSLContext.wrap_bio()` from anyio's `server_hostname`, which the stdlib re-encodes with IDNA 2003, so anyio must pass an IDNA 2008 encoding (`src/anyio/streams/tls.py:147-158`).
`pattern_fit`: `injection_only` — one behavioural sink reached by four public entry points; the `_core/_sockets.py` hunks are a pure refactor of already-IDNA-2008 `getaddrinfo`, so no O2 site and no O8 route.
Strongest lever: over-hardening — an unconditional `idna.encode()` breaks IP-literal/trailing-dot host names, while encoding in `connect_tcp()` alone leaves direct `TLSStream.wrap()`/`TLSConnectable` users unfixed.
Biggest red flag: `single_site` (plus `tiny_repo`) — the effective fix is one call site in a small library.
